articles.title: AI TOKENS COSTING TOO MUCH? THERE'S "HELP!..." FOR YOUR SPEND
articles.summary:
80% of companies are missing AI spend forecasts by 25% or more. This webinar [5] lays out how to get back on track.

Join August 13th at 10 a.m. Pacific for a conversation hosted by Ramp on catching runaway token spend before it happens with automated visibility and control. You'll see how to implement spend limits on a central dashboard that tracks AI billing across providers, models, API keys, and teams.

Plus, by joining you have a chance to win a pair of Meta Glasses [6]🕶️

articles.title: US SENATE ADVANCES CLARITY ACT AHEAD OF AUGUST RECESS
articles.summary: Senate Majority Leader John Thune moved to set up a procedural vote on the CLARITY Act for when lawmakers return in September, giving the crypto market structure bill a path toward the Senate floor. The legislation would establish the first comprehensive federal framework for digital assets, but passage still depends on securing at least 60 votes amid Democratic concerns over government officials' crypto interests and ongoing disputes with banks over stablecoin rewards.

articles.title: EX-NUBANK EXECS LAUNCH AI WEALTH MANAGER DECADE FOLLOWING $85M SEED ROUND
articles.summary: Decade has emerged from stealth with an $85 million seed round backed by Greenoaks, Benchmark, and Diffusion to build an AI-native wealth management platform in Brazil. Founded by former Nubank CTO Vitor Olivier and Hyperplane founder Felipe Meneses, the company combines proprietary financial AI agents with human advisors to monitor portfolios, consolidate financial data, and deliver personalized investment guidance.

articles.title: JPMORGAN TO DEPLOY $750B FOR AFFORDABLE HOUSING BY 2035
articles.summary: JPMorgan plans to help build or preserve 1 million lower-cost homes and support 500,000 homebuyers, including 200,000 first-time buyers. The bank expects to increase mortgage lending by roughly 40% and hire 850 home lending advisers while partnering with developers, nonprofits, and governments to expand housing supply.

articles.title: FINANCIAL FIRMS PUT AI TO WORK ACROSS 27 TASKS, STUDY FINDS
articles.summary: Large financial institutions are deploying AI most aggressively in back office operations, with revenue recognition, credit risk assessment, and sales forecasting emerging as the most widely adopted use cases. A study found that 85% of financial firms plan to increase AI spending over the next year, while customer-facing applications remain limited as banks prioritize measurable outcomes, regulatory compliance, and human oversight.

articles.title: BLOCK'S DORSEY EVANGELIZES AI REORGANIZATION FOR FINANCIAL SERVICES
articles.summary: Block beat Wall Street's earnings estimates and raised its full-year outlook, crediting AI with helping the company develop and ship products faster. Following a 40% workforce reduction earlier this year, the fintech is leaning on AI to operate more efficiently while exploring ways to monetize new tools such as its Buzz development platform.

articles.title: BLOCK EXPLORES HOW TO PRICE AI
articles.summary: Block has deployed AI assistants across Cash App and Square but is deliberately holding off on monetization. CEO Jack Dorsey is prioritizing adoption and product quality before committing to a pricing model. Six months after cutting 40% of its workforce in an AI-focused reorg, agentic AI now writes and reviews nearly all of Block's production code. Q2 gross profit rose 25% to $3.2B.

articles.title: NOT ALL MCPS ARE CREATED EQUAL
articles.summary: Brex argues that “MCP support” is a misleading checkbox because implementations differ dramatically in scalability, accuracy, latency, and permissioning. The company says its architecture continuously pre-computes and denormalizes finance data so agents can query large datasets in seconds with database-calculated answers, while reserving a slower conversational layer for ambiguous questions that require interpretation.

articles.title: LIGHTSPEED LEADS $37M SERIES A TO AUTOMATE INTERNAL AUDIT
articles.summary: Lightspeed is leading a $37M Series A in Andera, an AI-native platform automating internal audit end-to-end, from SOX control testing to workpaper generation. The thesis: audit is a reasoning problem that rules engines never cracked, public companies spend $3M to $20M+ annually on audit fees, and the Big Four face an innovator's dilemma since their hourly billing model prevents them from cannibalizing themselves with AI.

articles.title: META IS ORDERED TO PAY $942 MILLION OVER CHILD SAFETY HARMS
articles.summary: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $942 million after finding the company failed to adequately protect children on Facebook and Instagram, including $567 million for youth treatment and prevention programs on top of $375 million in civil penalties. The ruling also requires new child safety measures such as improved AI-based age estimation, hidden like counts for minors, better reporting tools for schools, and greater transparency around platform risks. Meta plans to appeal, but the decision marks the first trial victory by a US state against a major technology company over child safety and could influence similar lawsuits across the country.

articles.title: MAJOR HEDGE FUNDS TARGETED IN WAVE OF ATTEMPTED CYBER ATTACKS
articles.summary: Hackers launched a coordinated wave of AI-enabled voice phishing attacks against major hedge funds including Point72, Millennium Management, Two Sigma, and Citadel, highlighting the growing cybersecurity risks facing financial institutions. While firms reported little to no impact on client data, the attacks demonstrate how generative AI is making sophisticated social engineering campaigns cheaper, faster, and easier to scale across Wall Street. FINRA has increased information sharing with member firms as the industry braces for a new generation of AI-powered cyber threats.

articles.title: AMBROOK RAISES $30M TO EXPAND BEYOND FARMS INTO THE “REAL ECONOMY”
articles.summary: Ambrook raised a $30 million Series B led by Lachy Groom to expand its accounting and financial operations platform from agriculture into trucking, construction, and real estate, where many businesses still rely on paper or legacy tools like QuickBooks.

articles.title: FAYE RAISES $50M SERIES C TO EXPAND AI-POWERED TRAVEL PROTECTION
articles.summary: Faye raised $50 million in a Series C led by Madrona, bringing total funding to $100 million as it expands internationally, deepens partnerships with travel platforms, and invests further in AI-driven underwriting, assistance, and claims.
